title: Multi-zone egress contraction: simulation notes and operator playbook
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the simulation exercise and the resulting operator playbook for a controlled multi-zone egress contraction (aka staged capacity contraction) applied to a region whose upstream bandwidth or egress fabric is constrained. The goal: safely reduce regional egress capacity while maintaining KV cache locality, avoiding DNS TTL oscillation, and keeping tail latencies within SLOs.

Why this is different from a full regional failover:
- We are not evacuating compute or failing the region. We are intentionally throttling egress (outbound traffic) or shifting a fraction of traffic to other regions because the region's egress path (transit/peering/edge) is degraded or billing/capacity limited.
- This is lower-impact but more delicate: partial traffic shifts can cause oscillation, cache churn, and client-side reconnection storms if done too fast.

Simulation setup (Feb 2025 lab):
- Topology: three active regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west). Target region for contraction: us-west.
- Workload: mixed chat + embeddings + streaming, request mix matched to production 24h window.
- Keys: realistic KV cache hit distribution seeded with small and large prefixes.
- Routing stack: global controller -> region router -> edge proxies. We tested two mechanisms: weighted route adjustments (controller) and egress circuit-breaker that rewrites egress weights at the edge.
- DNS TTLs: 30s/120s/600s scenarios tested.

Key simulation findings:
- Fast shifts (>50% weight change within <60s) caused pronounced cache churn: p95 latency increased 2.6x for affected prefixes and embedding tail errors spiked.
- Staggered 10% per-5min reductions with kvcache preseed (warmup proxy to new region) maintained p95 within SLO in 4/5 runs.
- DNS TTL <= 60s helped client reconvergence for connection-heavy mobile clients but increased load on control plane; a 120s TTL was the operational sweet spot for most web clients.
- Circuit-breaker triggers based on egress BW (Gbps) + sustained error rate gave cleaner automated protection than purely latency-based triggers.
- Observed risk: if controller weight updates are not sequentialized with kvcache-warmup, races can create ~1–3 minute windows of double misses.

Operator playbook (for an SRE oncall):
Preconditions (what to check before starting):
- Confirm upstream provider alert or billing signal and the expected duration (Slack/Provider portal).
- Notify #sre-oncall and product incident channel with short note (template below).
- Verify global controller health: controller-api OK, route-persistence writes OK.
- Confirm kvcache rehydration workers are online and not overloaded (kvcache-worker-pods > 2, queue backlog < 500).
- Verify we have recent snapshots of prefix distributions (last 6h).

Step 0: quick experiment (small blast)
- Purpose: sanity-check automations and dashboards before larger changes.
- Action: decrease us-west egress weight by 5% (controller API) for 30s, then roll back. Observe: p95 latency, error rate, kvcache-hit-rate and edge CPU.
- If any metric degrades > 2x baseline or error rate > 1% absolute, abort and escalate to SRE leads.

Step 1: enable contract-mode (manual guided)
- Target cadence: -10 percentage points of egress weight every 5 minutes. Example sequence: 100 -> 90 -> 80 -> 70 ...
- Command (controller): curl -X POST https://controller.internal/v1/routes/adjust -d '{"region":"us-west","weight_delta":-10}' (operator: use internal CLI script which wraps auth).
- After each change, wait 3 full minutes; verify: p95 < SLO+10%, error_rate < baseline+0.5%, kvcache_hit_rate drop < 10% relative.

Step 2: preseed kvcache for target regions
- Kick off rehydration job for prefixes expected to migrate: infra/kvcache/rehydrate --source=us-west --targets=us-east,eu-west --prefix-list=top-10k
- Ensure rehydrate job shows progress: items_in_flight < 500, estimated completion < 20m for large runs.
- If rehydration is slow, reduce contraction cadence (e.g., -5% per 10 minutes).

Step 3: coordinate DNS and edge connection draining
- If we need to accelerate client reconvergence for non-streaming traffic, reduce DNS TTL to 120s for the affected global records (DNS admin console).
- For streaming-heavy endpoints, use connection-level drain via edge (edge-proxy drain rate 5 connections/sec) rather than dropping existing long-lived connections.
- Confirm CDN/edge caching invalidation windows for any cached artifacts.

Step 4: monitor and apply safety rollbacks
- Safety circuit-breaker checks (automated but operator can force):
  - If p99 latency increases > 50% for > 3 consecutive minutes -> pause contraction and incrementally revert last step.
  - If region error rate > 3% absolute -> immediate rollback of last two steps and notify engineering leads.
  - If kvcache miss rate > 25% relative for > 10 minutes -> pause and consider targeted re-seed of hottest prefixes.
- Rollback command: controller adjust with positive weight_delta to restore previous weights; kick off targeted kvcache preseed to reduce miss storm.

Telemetry and dashboards to watch (quick checklist):
- control-plane/routes/weights (recent writes + applied weights)
- edge/egress/gbps/us-west, us-east, eu-west (real-time + 1m/5m)
- requests/p95/p99 per-region and per-route
- requests/error-rate per-region and per-route
- kvcache/hit-rate and kvcache/rehydration/queue-length
- client/reconnect-rate and active-connections by region
- infra/edge-proxy-cpu and router-apply-latency (controller->edge propagation)
- alerting: SLO-latency, SLO-error-rate, kvcache-miss-critical

Automation scripts and locations:
- Internal CLI: infra/tools/route-adjust (wraps controller API + dry-run mode)
- Kvcache rehydrate job: infra/kvcache/rehydrate (k8s job template infra/kvcache/rehydrate.yaml)
- Canary simulator (lab): infra/sim/egress-contraction-sim with presets in infra/sim/presets/multi-zone-2025-02.json
- Runbook helper play (PagerDuty): scripts/playbooks/egress-contract-notify.sh (posts to Slack + triggers PD if thresholds hit)

Post-action: graceful recovery and cleanup:
- After provider healthy or capacity restored, reverse steps at a symmetric cadence (+10% per 5 minutes) while re-checking metrics.
- Revert DNS TTL to production default (600s) only after majority of active clients have reconnected (monitor client reconverge).
- Run a postmortem within 72 hours if playbook executed beyond experimental quick-blast. Include: timeline, decisions, metrics, and concrete action items.

Open questions & follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Q1: Can controller apply weight deltas as a transactional sequence to avoid races with kvcache rehydration? (owner: Aaron Cho, ticket SRE-3490)
- Q2: Add automated hottest-prefix preseed step when contraction > 20% to reduce kvcache churn (owner: Lena Kim, GH PR referenced).
- Q3: Test interaction with mobile clients with 15s DNS TTL edge-case (owner: Marcus Li, lab test next sprint).
- Q4: Disaster-mode fallback: should we run a hard evacuation play if contraction fails after 3 iterations? Define criteria (owner: Priya Desai).

Run notes from Feb 2025 simulation (raw):
- Run A: 10% every 5m, kvcache preseed enabled. Result: stable, small spike in p95 (~12%) on step 3.
- Run B: 25% immediate drop. Result: kvcache miss storms, p99 x3, required emergency rollback.
- Run C: 5% every 2m without preseed. Result: edge CPU spike + control-plane write queue backlog -> slowed updates and oscillation.

Communication templates (short):
- Incident start (Slack): [SRE] US-WEST egress constrained, initiating phased contraction. Expect 30-60m. Will post updates every step. PD oncall: @pd-sre
- Escalation: [SRE-URGENT] contraction paused due to p99 spike > 50% for 3m. Rolling back last step.

Action items (immediate):
- Aaron: implement transactional controller weight API prototype (due 2025-02-28).
- Lena: open PR to add hottest-prefix preseed to rehydrate job (link in linked_artifacts).
- Marcus: schedule mobile-client TTL lab test (due next lab sprint).
- Priya: draft postmortem template and incident timeline skeleton.

Appendix: quick operator cheatsheet (copy-paste commands)
- Dry-run weight adjust: infra/tools/route-adjust --region us-west --delta -10 --dry-run
- Apply weight adjust: infra/tools/route-adjust --region us-west --delta -10
- Start kvcache rehydrate: kubectl -n infra apply -f infra/kvcache/rehydrate.yaml --record
- Force rollback to 100%: infra/tools/route-adjust --region us-west --set 100 --force

Notes to self: keep this doc iterative. Add more real incident logs after next live run. Avoid lowering DNS TTL below 120s unless absolutely necessary (mobile special case).

References:
- SRE-3421: provider-egress-throttle-alerts
- Confluence playbook draft (link above)
- infra PR 812 (kvcache rehydrate tuning)

End of draft.
